intended_object: The pure braid group P_n: the kernel of the natural surjection B_n → S_n that sends each braid to the permutation it induces on the strands, i.e. the braids that return every strand to its own position. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
`BraidGroup n` is the Artin group of type A_{n-1}. This is the standard Artin presentation of B_n, with generators σ_1, …, σ_{n-1}, distant commutation and the braid relation for neighbours. `permHom n` is defined through the universal property: it sends σ_i to the adjacent transposition (i i+1) in `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`. This is the standard map B_n → S_n, and the library proves it surjective.

`pureSubgroup n` is the kernel of `permHom n`, which is exactly the textbook definition of the pure braid group P_n. The degenerate cases come out right: for n = 0 and n = 1 the braid group is trivial (`A (n-1)` is `A 0`, which has no generators), and so is P_n.

The Artin-group generalisation (the pure Artin group, i.e. the kernel to the Coxeter group) is a different named notion. The pure braid group itself is defined at its natural generality. Mathlib has no braid groups or pure braid groups, so it has no counterpart.
